title: Cost Accounting II
topics: Cost accounting systems and the cost ledger

items.q: A contract has a price of N4500000. The surveyor has certified 60 percent of the work. What is the value of work certified?
items.s: Value certified = contract price x rate/100 = 4500000 x 60/100 = 2700000 naira.

items.q: Work certified on a contract is N3600000 and the agreement provides for retention of 15 percent. How much is held back?
items.s: Retention = 3600000 x 15/100 = 540000 naira.

items.q: Budgeted sales are 8000 units. Opening finished stock is 600 units and closing finished stock is budgeted at 1200 units. What is the production budget in units?
items.s: Production = sales + closing stock - opening stock = 8000 + 1200 - 600 = 8600 units.

items.q: A budget provides for 9000 units, each needing 4 direct labour hours at N150 an hour. What is the direct labour budget?
items.s: Labour budget = 9000 x 4 x 150 = 5400000 naira.

items.q: A product sells for N180 and its variable cost is N110 a unit. What is the contribution per unit?
items.s: Contribution = selling price - variable cost = 180 - 110 = 70 naira.

items.q: A vehicle has a standing charge of N750000 a year and a running cost of N20 a kilometre. It is expected to cover 20000 kilometres. What is the total operating cost for the year?
items.s: Total cost = standing charge + running cost x distance = 750000 + 20 x 20000 = 1150000 naira.

items.q: The full cost of a component is N100 and the transfer pricing rule is full cost plus 20 percent. What is the transfer price?
items.s: Transfer price = full cost x (100 + mark-up)/100 = 100 x (100 + 20)/100 = 120 naira.

items.q: The cost ledger control account opens with a credit balance of N320000. Costs put through the account during the period were N1700000 and amounts taken out to the financial ledger were N1600000. What is the closing credit balance?
items.s: Closing balance = opening balance + costs put through - amounts taken out = 320000 + 1700000 - 1600000 = 420000 naira.
items.t: Cost accounting systems and the cost ledger

items.q: A branch trades in premises owned by the firm. A notional rent of N240000 a year is charged in the branch records although no money is paid. Before this charge the branch shows a profit of N1680000. What profit is left after it?
items.s: Profit after the notional charge = 1680000 - 240000 = 1440000 naira.
items.t: Cost accounting systems and the cost ledger

items.q: A plant makes 34000 units a year at a unit cost of N85. The cost reduction committee has set a target of cutting 4 percent from the total cost. What saving is being targeted?
items.s: Saving = units x unit cost x rate/100 = 34000 x 85 x 4/100 = 115600 naira.

items.q: A process starts with 2000 units at a total cost of N750000. Normal loss is 8 percent of input and the waste sells for N10 a unit. Actual output was 1288 units. What is the value of the abnormal loss?
items.s: Expected good output = 2000 - 160 = 1840 units, cost per good unit = (750000 - 160 x 10)/1840 = 406.74; abnormal loss = (1840 - 1288) x 406.74 = 224520 naira.

items.q: A process receives 5000 units at a total cost of N640000. Normal loss is 12 percent of input and the waste sells for N20 a unit. Actual output was 4620 units. What is the value of the abnormal gain?
items.s: Expected good output = 5000 - 600 = 4400 units, cost per good unit = (640000 - 600 x 20)/4400 = 142.73; abnormal gain = (4620 - 4400) x 142.73 = 31400 naira.

items.q: In a process 2400 units were completed and transferred out. Closing work in progress was 600 units, 40 percent complete. What are the equivalent units of output?
items.s: Equivalent units = completed + work in progress x degree of completion = 2400 + 600 x 40/100 = 2640.

items.q: A process incurs costs of N600000 on 2000 units. Normal loss is 10 percent of input and each lost unit is sold for N20. What is the cost per good unit?
items.s: Good output = 2000 - 200 = 1800 units; net cost = 600000 - 200 x 20 = 596000; cost per good unit = 331.11.

items.q: Joint costs of N900000 produced 3000 units of product A selling at N80 and 2000 units of product B selling at N120. Using the sales value method, what joint cost is charged to product A?

Joint costs of N640000 were incurred. Product A: 4000 units sell at N120 after further costs of N40000. Product B: 2000 units sell at N150 after further costs of N40000. Under the net realisable value method, what joint cost is charged to product A?
Joint costs of N960000 produced a main product and a by-product. The by-product sells for N40000 and costs N10000 to sell. What joint cost is charged to the main product?
items.s: Joint cost of the main product = 960000 - (40000 - 10000) = 930000 naira.

items.q: Joint costs of N720000 produced 6000 kilograms of product A and 2000 kilograms of product B. Using the physical units method, what joint cost is charged to product A?
Work certified is N2000000 and retention is 10 percent. The customer has paid everything except the retention. What cash has been received?
Cost incurred on a contract to date is N3400000, of which N120000 relates to work not yet certified. What is the cost of work certified?
items.s: Cost of work certified = 3400000 - 120000 = 3280000 naira.

items.q: Notional profit on a contract is N540000. Work certified is N1800000 and cash received is N1300000. The firm takes credit for the part of notional profit that cash received bears to work certified. What profit is taken?
Work certified is N3600000 with retention of 5 percent. The customer has already paid N1500000. What amount is still due from the customer?
items.s: Still due = 3600000 - retention (3600000 x 5/100 = 180000) - already paid 1500000 = 1920000 naira.

items.q: The standard price of a material is N30 a unit and 5000 units were bought at N22 each. What is the material price variance, taking a saving as positive and an excess as negative?
items.s: Price variance = (standard - actual) x quantity bought = (30 - 22) x 5000 = 40000 naira.

items.q: The standard input for the output produced is 4800 units at a standard price of N40. Actual input used was 4000 units. What is the material usage variance, taking a saving as positive and an excess as negative?
items.s: Usage variance = (standard quantity - actual quantity) x standard price = (4800 - 4000) x 40 = 32000 naira.

items.q: The standard wage rate is N100 an hour and 1200 hours were worked, paid at N125 an hour. What is the labour rate variance, taking a saving as positive and an excess as negative?
items.s: Rate variance = (standard rate - actual rate) x hours paid = (100 - 125) x 1200 = -30000 naira.

items.q: The standard hours for the output produced are 1400 and 1750 hours were actually worked. The standard rate is N100 an hour. What is the labour efficiency variance, taking a saving as positive and an excess as negative?
items.s: Efficiency variance = (standard hours - actual hours) x standard rate = (1400 - 1750) x 100 = -35000 naira.

items.q: Budgeted overhead for a department is N900000 for 30000 machine hours. In the period 26000 hours were worked. How much overhead was absorbed?
items.s: Absorption rate = 900000/30000 = 30 per hour; absorbed = 30 x 26000 = 780000 naira.

items.q: Budgeted overhead is N600000 for 30000 machine hours. Actual hours worked were 33000 and actual overhead incurred was N700000. What is the over or under absorption, taking over absorption as positive and under absorption as negative?
items.s: Absorption rate = 600000/30000 = 20; absorbed = 20 x 33000 = 660000; over or under = 660000 - 700000 = -40000 naira.

items.q: The production budget is 7500 units and each unit needs 4 kilograms of material. Opening raw material is 1200 kilograms and closing raw material is 3000 kilograms. What is the purchase budget in kilograms?
items.s: Usage = 7500 x 4 = 30000 kg; purchases = usage + closing - opening = 30000 + 3000 - 1200 = 31800 kg.

items.q: At a budgeted volume of 5000 units the variable cost is N40 a unit and fixed cost is N240000. What total cost should be allowed if 7000 units are actually made?
items.s: Allowed cost = variable x actual units + fixed = 40 x 7000 + 240000 = 520000 naira.

items.q: Fixed costs are N660000 and the contribution per unit is N40. What is the break-even point in units?
items.s: Break-even units = fixed cost/contribution per unit = 660000/40 = 16500 units.

items.q: Fixed costs are N480000 and the profit-volume ratio is 40 percent. What is the break-even sales value?
items.s: Break-even sales = fixed cost/(profit-volume ratio/100) = 480000/(40/100) = 1200000 naira.

items.q: Actual sales are N2400000 and break-even sales are N1500000. What is the margin of safety as a percentage of actual sales?
Fixed costs are N480000, contribution per unit is N40 and the profit target is N240000. How many units must be sold?
items.s: Units = (fixed cost + target profit)/contribution per unit = (480000 + 240000)/40 = 18000 units.

items.q: Each unit needs 4 hours of a skilled grade. Only 8000 such hours are available and the contribution is N60 a unit. Fixed costs are N90000. What is the greatest profit the firm can make?
items.s: Units possible = 8000/4 = 2000; contribution earned = 2000 x 60 = 120000; profit = 120000 - 90000 = 30000 naira.

items.q: A component can be made in house or bought outside. Making it would need a special machine hired at N210000 and variable costs of N380000. Fixed overhead of N160000 would be incurred either way. What is the relevant cost of making it?
items.s: Relevant cost = avoidable hire + variable cost = 210000 + 380000 = 590000 naira; the fixed overhead is common to both choices.

items.q: Budgeted production overhead is N600000 and budgeted direct labour hours are 16000. What is the overhead absorption rate per direct labour hour?
items.s: Absorption rate = 600000/16000 = 37.5 naira per hour.

items.q: Rent of N750000 is shared between two departments on floor area. Department A occupies 1800 square metres and department B occupies 1000 square metres. What rent is charged to department A?
A support activity has a cost pool of N360000 and is driven by 1200 setups. Under activity based costing, what is the rate per setup?
items.s: Rate per setup = 360000/1200 = 300 naira.

items.q: A service department's costs of N1100000 are apportioned 50 percent to production department A and 40 percent to production department B. What total is charged to the two production departments?
items.s: Charge to production = 1100000 x (100 - 50 - 40)/100 = 110000 naira.

items.q: A bus covers 120000 kilometres in a year. Running cost is N22 a kilometre and the fixed cost for the year is N600000. What is the cost per kilometre?
A haulage firm carries 40 tonnes of load over 250 kilometres at a total cost of N720000. What is the cost per tonne-kilometre?
items.s: Tonne-kilometres = 40 x 250 = 10000; cost per unit = 720000/10000 = 72 naira.

items.q: A division earns a profit of N600000 on assets employed of N4000000. What is the return on investment, as a percentage?
items.s: Return on investment = 600000/4000000 x 100 = 15 percent.

items.q: A division earns a profit of N600000 on assets of N5000000. The firm charges 8 percent on the assets employed. What is the residual income?
items.s: Residual income = profit - charge = 600000 - (5000000 x 8/100) = 200000 naira.

items.q: A product must sell at N360 a unit to remain competitive and the firm requires a margin of 25 percent on selling price. What is the target cost per unit?
items.s: Allowed revenue is the price itself; target cost = 360 x (100 - 25)/100 = 270 naira.

items.q: A process receives 2500 units. Normal loss is 10 percent of input and each lost unit can be sold for N10. What amount is credited to the process for the expected waste?
items.s: Waste = 2500 x 10/100 = 250 units; scrap credit = 250 x 10 = 2500 naira.

items.q: Work certified on a contract is N3000000 and the agreement provides for retention of 10 percent. How much is held back?
items.s: Retention = 3000000 x 10/100 = 300000 naira.

items.q: Budgeted sales are 9500 units. Opening finished stock is 1000 units and closing finished stock is budgeted at 1200 units. What is the production budget in units?
items.s: Production = sales + closing stock - opening stock = 9500 + 1200 - 1000 = 9700 units.

items.q: A budget provides for 8000 units, each needing 4 direct labour hours at N180 an hour. What is the direct labour budget?
items.s: Labour budget = 8000 x 4 x 180 = 5760000 naira.

items.q: A product sells for N180 and its variable cost is N70 a unit. What is the contribution per unit?
items.s: Contribution = selling price - variable cost = 180 - 70 = 110 naira.

items.q: A vehicle has a standing charge of N750000 a year and a running cost of N20 a kilometre. It is expected to cover 25000 kilometres. What is the total operating cost for the year?
items.s: Total cost = standing charge + running cost x distance = 750000 + 20 x 25000 = 1250000 naira.

items.q: The full cost of a component is N120 and the transfer pricing rule is full cost plus 10 percent. What is the transfer price?
items.s: Transfer price = full cost x (100 + mark-up)/100 = 120 x (100 + 10)/100 = 132 naira.

items.q: The cost ledger control account opens with a credit balance of N180000. Costs put through the account during the period were N1200000 and amounts taken out to the financial ledger were N880000. What is the closing credit balance?
items.s: Closing balance = opening balance + costs put through - amounts taken out = 180000 + 1200000 - 880000 = 500000 naira.
items.t: Cost accounting systems and the cost ledger

items.q: A branch trades in premises owned by the firm. A notional rent of N480000 a year is charged in the branch records although no money is paid. Before this charge the branch shows a profit of N1420000. What profit is left after it?
items.s: Profit after the notional charge = 1420000 - 480000 = 940000 naira.
items.t: Cost accounting systems and the cost ledger

items.q: A plant makes 25000 units a year at a unit cost of N85. The cost reduction committee has set a target of cutting 10 percent from the total cost. What saving is being targeted?
items.s: Saving = units x unit cost x rate/100 = 25000 x 85 x 10/100 = 212500 naira.

items.q: A process starts with 3000 units at a total cost of N480000. Normal loss is 5 percent of input and the waste sells for N20 a unit. Actual output was 1710 units. What is the value of the abnormal loss?
items.s: Expected good output = 3000 - 150 = 2850 units, cost per good unit = (480000 - 150 x 20)/2850 = 167.37; abnormal loss = (2850 - 1710) x 167.37 = 190800 naira.

items.q: A process receives 3000 units at a total cost of N400000. Normal loss is 5 percent of input and the waste sells for N20 a unit. Actual output was 2992 units. What is the value of the abnormal gain?
items.s: Expected good output = 3000 - 150 = 2850 units, cost per good unit = (400000 - 150 x 20)/2850 = 139.3; abnormal gain = (2992 - 2850) x 139.3 = 19780.35 naira.

items.q: In a process 2000 units were completed and transferred out. Closing work in progress was 400 units, 75 percent complete. What are the equivalent units of output?
items.s: Equivalent units = completed + work in progress x degree of completion = 2000 + 400 x 75/100 = 2300.

items.q: A process incurs costs of N720000 on 4000 units. Normal loss is 10 percent of input and each lost unit is sold for N20. What is the cost per good unit?
items.s: Good output = 4000 - 400 = 3600 units; net cost = 720000 - 400 x 20 = 712000; cost per good unit = 197.78.

items.q: Joint costs of N750000 produced 4000 units of product A selling at N60 and 1000 units of product B selling at N140. Using the sales value method, what joint cost is charged to product A?
Which statement correctly defines equivalent units?
o: a measure that converts partly finished work into the number of complete items it equals
apportioning common outlay in the ratio of what each output fetches
the waste that ordinary working conditions make unavoidable in a process
a future outlay that differs between the choices open to the firm
items.s: equivalent units: a measure that converts partly finished work into the number of complete items it equals. The other options describe relevant cost, normal loss, sales value method.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines adverse variance?
o: money set aside at intervals to meet the expected cost of repairs
the outlay on stages finished but not yet approved for payment
the spreading of indirect outlay over output so that each item carries a share
a gap that reduces profit compared with the plan
items.s: adverse variance: a gap that reduces profit compared with the plan. The other options describe maintenance provision, work uncertified, absorption.

items.q: life cycle costing may be defined as
o: setting the allowable outlay by deducting the wanted profit from the price the market will pay
keeping spending within the limits already set for it
gathering all outlay on an item from design through to withdrawal from use
working out the outlay of a unit of help given rather than of goods made
items.s: life cycle costing: gathering all outlay on an item from design through to withdrawal from use. The other options describe target costing, service costing, cost control.

items.q: Which of the following best describes work certified?
o: a gap that reduces profit compared with the plan
the value of finished stages that the customer surveyor has approved
an amount brought into the costing records for something the firm uses but does not pay for
the level of activity at which neither profit nor loss arises
items.s: work certified: the value of finished stages that the customer surveyor has approved. The other options describe break-even point, adverse variance, notional charge.

items.q: Which term is described by “a schedule that explains why two sets of records show different results for one period”?
o: uniform costing
cost ledger control account
integrated system
reconciliation statement
items.s: reconciliation statement is a schedule that explains why two sets of records show different results for one period.
items.t: Cost accounting systems and the cost ledger

items.q: Which of the following best describes abnormal gain?
o: the proportion of the carrying capacity actually used
spending incurred after the outputs have become distinct and traceable to one of them
output above the expected level, credited to the process at the same rate as the expected waste
an amount brought into the costing records for something the firm uses but does not pay for
items.s: abnormal gain: output above the expected level, credited to the process at the same rate as the expected waste. The other options describe vehicle utilisation, separable cost, notional charge.

items.q: Which of the following best describes cost driver?
o: the planned indirect outlay of a department divided by its planned activity
the measure of activity that makes a support outlay arise
a measure that converts partly finished work into the number of complete items it equals
working out the outlay of a unit of help given rather than of goods made
items.s: cost driver: the measure of activity that makes a support outlay arise. The other options describe absorption rate, service costing, equivalent units.

items.q: notional charge may be defined as
o: the length of the stretch of activity a plan is drawn to cover
outlay that varies with the distance covered
an amount brought into the costing records for something the firm uses but does not pay for
the resource in shortest supply that holds back the level of activity
items.s: notional charge: an amount brought into the costing records for something the firm uses but does not pay for. The other options describe limiting factor, budget period, running cost.
items.t: Cost accounting systems and the cost ledger

items.q: Which of the following best describes scrap value?
o: the amount realisable by selling waste material
a term allowing the agreed sum to rise if input prices increase
working out the outlay of a unit of help given rather than of goods made
the amount actually collected from the customer so far
items.s: scrap value: the amount realisable by selling waste material. The other options describe cash received, escalation clause, service costing.

items.q: Which term is described by “outlay that varies with the distance covered”?
o: service costing
running cost
operating cost statement
vehicle utilisation
items.s: running cost is outlay that varies with the distance covered.

items.q: All of the following belong to Process costing and losses EXCEPT
o: normal loss
passenger journey
abnormal loss
abnormal gain
items.s: Every other option belongs to Process costing and losses. “passenger journey” belongs to Service costing and cost units, not Process costing and losses.

items.q: The statement “a plan redrawn at the level of activity actually reached” describes which of the following?
o: cash budget
flexible budget
production budget
purchase budget
items.s: flexible budget is a plan redrawn at the level of activity actually reached.

items.q: The statement “sales value less the variable outlay of the items sold” describes which of the following?
o: contribution
margin of safety
relevant cost
break-even point
items.s: contribution is sales value less the variable outlay of the items sold.

items.q: Which of the following best describes value analysis?
o: a gap that increases profit compared with the plan
the record that gathers the input of one stage and shows the output transferred onward
examining what each part of an item does in order to remove needless outlay
the measure of activity that makes a support outlay arise
items.s: value analysis: examining what each part of an item does in order to remove needless outlay. The other options describe process account, favourable variance, cost driver.

items.q: Which term is described by “the outlay on the stages that the surveyor has approved”?
o: work certified
work uncertified
cost of work certified
cash received
items.s: cost of work certified is the outlay on the stages that the surveyor has approved.

items.q: The statement “the total sum agreed with the customer for completing the job” describes which of the following?
o: contract price
retention money
notional profit
work certified
items.s: contract price is the total sum agreed with the customer for completing the job.

items.q: Which of the following best describes degree of completion?
o: the proportion of the processing on partly finished items that has already been carried out
sales value less the variable outlay of the items sold
the amount actually collected from the customer so far
building every plan from nothing so that each item must be justified afresh
items.s: degree of completion: the proportion of the processing on partly finished items that has already been carried out. The other options describe zero-based budgeting, contribution, cash received.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines degree of completion?
o: the resource in shortest supply that holds back the level of activity
the proportion of the processing on partly finished items that has already been carried out
the effect of using more or less input than the recipe allows, valued at the planned rate
the pattern in which the hours needed per item fall by a fixed proportion as output doubles
items.s: degree of completion: the proportion of the processing on partly finished items that has already been carried out. The other options describe material usage variance, limiting factor, learning curve.

items.q: sales value method may be defined as
o: the outlay on the stages that the surveyor has approved
charging indirect outlay to items according to the demands each makes on support work
the excess of the approved value over the outlay on the stages approved
apportioning common outlay in the ratio of what each output fetches
items.s: sales value method: apportioning common outlay in the ratio of what each output fetches. The other options describe activity based costing, cost of work certified, notional profit.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines profit-volume ratio?
o: the effect of using more or less input than the recipe allows, valued at the planned rate
a measure that converts partly finished work into the number of complete items it equals
contribution expressed as a percentage of sales value
a future outlay that differs between the choices open to the firm
items.s: profit-volume ratio: contribution expressed as a percentage of sales value. The other options describe equivalent units, material usage variance, relevant cost.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines reconciliation statement?
o: a schedule that explains why two sets of records show different results for one period
apportioning common outlay in the ratio of what each output fetches
the value of finished stages that the customer surveyor has approved
the extra outlay caused by making one more item
items.s: reconciliation statement: a schedule that explains why two sets of records show different results for one period. The other options describe work certified, marginal cost, sales value method.
items.t: Cost accounting systems and the cost ledger

items.q: budgetary control may be defined as
o: spending incurred after the outputs have become distinct and traceable to one of them
the setting of plans, the comparison of actual with plan, and action on the differences
two separate sets of records kept in agreement by a pair of mirror accounts
the length of the stretch of activity a plan is drawn to cover
items.s: budgetary control: the setting of plans, the comparison of actual with plan, and action on the differences. The other options describe separable cost, interlocking system, budget period.

items.q: budget may be defined as
o: a quantified plan for a defined period, expressed in money or in quantity
gathering all outlay on an item from design through to withdrawal from use
the effect of using more or less input than the recipe allows, valued at the planned rate
a measure that converts partly finished work into the number of complete items it equals
items.s: budget: a quantified plan for a defined period, expressed in money or in quantity. The other options describe equivalent units, material usage variance, life cycle costing.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines cash budget?
o: a future outlay that differs between the choices open to the firm
a gap that increases profit compared with the plan
a forecast of money coming in and going out and of the balance left
the effect of using more or less input than the recipe allows, valued at the planned rate
items.s: cash budget: a forecast of money coming in and going out and of the balance left. The other options describe relevant cost, favourable variance, material usage variance.

items.q: The statement “building every plan from nothing so that each item must be justified afresh” describes which of the following?
o: purchase budget
budgetary control
zero-based budgeting
cash budget
items.s: zero-based budgeting is building every plan from nothing so that each item must be justified afresh.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines vehicle utilisation.
o: the proportion of the carrying capacity actually used
a schedule that gathers the fixed and variable outlay of a fleet for a period
apportioning on selling price less the further spending needed to complete and sell
the extra outlay caused by making one more item
items.s: vehicle utilisation: the proportion of the carrying capacity actually used. The other options describe marginal cost, operating cost statement, net realisable value method.

items.q: Which term is described by “a future outlay that differs between the choices open to the firm”?
o: marginal cost
relevant cost
margin of safety
limiting factor
items.s: relevant cost is a future outlay that differs between the choices open to the firm.

items.q: adverse variance may be defined as
o: a real saving in the outlay of a unit without loss of quality
a working paper that spreads indirect outlay across the sections of a factory
the effect of using more or less input than the recipe allows, valued at the planned rate
a gap that reduces profit compared with the plan
items.s: adverse variance: a gap that reduces profit compared with the plan. The other options describe material usage variance, cost reduction, cost apportionment sheet.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines flexible budget.
o: money set aside at intervals to meet the expected cost of repairs
building every plan from nothing so that each item must be justified afresh
waste beyond the expected level, valued separately and kept out of the cost of good output
a plan redrawn at the level of activity actually reached
items.s: flexible budget: a plan redrawn at the level of activity actually reached. The other options describe maintenance provision, zero-based budgeting, abnormal loss.

items.q: The statement “a single set of records that serves both the financial and the costing purposes of the firm” describes which of the following?
o: integrated system
reconciliation statement
feedforward control
cost ledger control account
items.s: integrated system is a single set of records that serves both the financial and the costing purposes of the firm.
items.t: Cost accounting systems and the cost ledger

items.q: Which term is described by “the planned outlay for one item, built up from technical specifications”?
o: idle time variance
favourable variance
material price variance
standard cost
items.s: standard cost is the planned outlay for one item, built up from technical specifications.

items.q: composite cost unit may be defined as
o: a measure that combines two things, such as weight carried and distance covered
a future outlay that differs between the choices open to the firm
the extra outlay caused by making one more item
the length of the stretch of activity a plan is drawn to cover
items.s: composite cost unit: a measure that combines two things, such as weight carried and distance covered. The other options describe marginal cost, budget period, relevant cost.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines favourable variance.
o: contribution expressed as a percentage of sales value
the total sum agreed with the customer for completing the job
a gap that increases profit compared with the plan
the amount realisable by selling waste material
items.s: favourable variance: a gap that increases profit compared with the plan. The other options describe contract price, scrap value, profit-volume ratio.

items.q: Which of the following best describes budgetary control?
o: an amount brought into the costing records for something the firm uses but does not pay for
the amount realisable by selling waste material
the effect of using more or less input than the recipe allows, valued at the planned rate
the setting of plans, the comparison of actual with plan, and action on the differences
items.s: budgetary control: the setting of plans, the comparison of actual with plan, and action on the differences. The other options describe material usage variance, scrap value, notional charge.

items.q: Which of the following best describes budget?
o: setting the allowable outlay by deducting the wanted profit from the price the market will pay
the gap between a planned figure and the figure actually recorded
the proportion of the carrying capacity actually used
a quantified plan for a defined period, expressed in money or in quantity
items.s: budget: a quantified plan for a defined period, expressed in money or in quantity. The other options describe target costing, vehicle utilisation, variance.

items.q: separable cost may be defined as
o: the record in the costing books that mirrors the total of the financial books and keeps the two sets in step
setting the allowable outlay by deducting the wanted profit from the price the market will pay
the gap between a planned figure and the figure actually recorded
spending incurred after the outputs have become distinct and traceable to one of them
items.s: separable cost: spending incurred after the outputs have become distinct and traceable to one of them. The other options describe target costing, cost ledger control account, variance.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines learning curve?
o: a term allowing the agreed sum to rise if input prices increase
a real saving in the outlay of a unit without loss of quality
the pattern in which the hours needed per item fall by a fixed proportion as output doubles
keeping spending within the limits already set for it
items.s: learning curve: the pattern in which the hours needed per item fall by a fixed proportion as output doubles. The other options describe escalation clause, cost control, cost reduction.

items.q: Which term is described by “setting the allowable outlay by deducting the wanted profit from the price the market will pay”?
o: life cycle costing
target costing
cost reduction
learning curve
items.s: target costing is setting the allowable outlay by deducting the wanted profit from the price the market will pay.

items.q: Which term is described by “the shortfall of indirect outlay charged to output compared with what was incurred”?
o: under-absorption
cost driver
allocation
apportionment
items.s: under-absorption is the shortfall of indirect outlay charged to output compared with what was incurred.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines separable cost.
o: a gap that increases profit compared with the plan
spending incurred after the outputs have become distinct and traceable to one of them
the planned outlay for one item, built up from technical specifications
the proportion of the carrying capacity actually used
items.s: separable cost: spending incurred after the outputs have become distinct and traceable to one of them. The other options describe standard cost, vehicle utilisation, favourable variance.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines absorption.
o: a forecast of money coming in and going out and of the balance left
spending incurred after the outputs have become distinct and traceable to one of them
the spreading of indirect outlay over output so that each item carries a share
the level of activity at which neither profit nor loss arises
items.s: absorption: the spreading of indirect outlay over output so that each item carries a share. The other options describe break-even point, separable cost, cash budget.

items.q: passenger journey may be defined as
o: the carrying of one traveller over the whole route once
the shortfall of indirect outlay charged to output compared with what was incurred
the sharing of an outlay between sections on a stated basis
sales value less the variable outlay of the items sold
items.s: passenger journey: the carrying of one traveller over the whole route once. The other options describe under-absorption, apportionment, contribution.

items.q: All of the following belong to Budgetary control EXCEPT
o: production budget
operating cost statement
budget
budgetary control
items.s: Every other option belongs to Budgetary control. “operating cost statement” belongs to Service costing and cost units, not Budgetary control.

items.q: profit-volume ratio may be defined as
o: output above the expected level, credited to the process at the same rate as the expected waste
contribution expressed as a percentage of sales value
sales value less the variable outlay of the items sold
apportioning common outlay in proportion to weight, volume or count
items.s: profit-volume ratio: contribution expressed as a percentage of sales value. The other options describe contribution, physical units method, abnormal gain.

items.q: Which term is described by “a real saving in the outlay of a unit without loss of quality”?
o: cost control
life cycle costing
cost reduction
value analysis
items.s: cost reduction is a real saving in the outlay of a unit without loss of quality.

items.q: Which term is described by “the outlay on stages finished but not yet approved for payment”?
o: escalation clause
cost of work certified
work uncertified
cash received
items.s: work uncertified is the outlay on stages finished but not yet approved for payment.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines relevant cost?
o: a future outlay that differs between the choices open to the firm
measuring one result against the best practice found elsewhere
an amount brought into the costing records for something the firm uses but does not pay for
the waste that ordinary working conditions make unavoidable in a process
items.s: relevant cost: a future outlay that differs between the choices open to the firm. The other options describe normal loss, notional charge, benchmarking.

items.q: The statement “a measure that converts partly finished work into the number of complete items it equals” describes which of the following?
o: equivalent units
normal loss
abnormal gain
work in progress
items.s: equivalent units is a measure that converts partly finished work into the number of complete items it equals.

items.q: Which of the following best describes purchase budget?
o: the planned indirect outlay of a department divided by its planned activity
the quantity of input to be bought, from the usage and the change in holdings
keeping spending within the limits already set for it
the setting of plans, the comparison of actual with plan, and action on the differences
items.s: purchase budget: the quantity of input to be bought, from the usage and the change in holdings. The other options describe cost control, absorption rate, budgetary control.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines scrap value.
o: money set aside at intervals to meet the expected cost of repairs
the measure of activity that makes a support outlay arise
the amount realisable by selling waste material
the planned outlay for one item, built up from technical specifications
items.s: scrap value: the amount realisable by selling waste material. The other options describe standard cost, cost driver, maintenance provision.

items.q: Which term is described by “the level of activity at which neither profit nor loss arises”?
o: limiting factor
break-even point
margin of safety
contribution
items.s: break-even point is the level of activity at which neither profit nor loss arises.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines passenger journey.
o: the carrying of one traveller over the whole route once
the rate at which a plant turns input into saleable output
a gap that reduces profit compared with the plan
a gap that increases profit compared with the plan
items.s: passenger journey: the carrying of one traveller over the whole route once. The other options describe adverse variance, throughput, favourable variance.

items.q: Which term is described by “waste beyond the expected level, valued separately and kept out of the cost of good output”?
o: abnormal gain
abnormal loss
equivalent units
process account
items.s: abnormal loss is waste beyond the expected level, valued separately and kept out of the cost of good output.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines marginal cost.
o: the effect of using more or less input than the recipe allows, valued at the planned rate
the extra outlay caused by making one more item
the outlay on stages finished but not yet approved for payment
the value of finished stages that the customer surveyor has approved
items.s: marginal cost: the extra outlay caused by making one more item. The other options describe work uncertified, material usage variance, work certified.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines physical units method.
o: the charging of a whole item of outlay to the section that caused it
the value of finished stages that the customer surveyor has approved
sales value less the variable outlay of the items sold
apportioning common outlay in proportion to weight, volume or count
items.s: physical units method: apportioning common outlay in proportion to weight, volume or count. The other options describe allocation, contribution, work certified.

items.q: benchmarking may be defined as
o: the charging of a whole item of outlay to the section that caused it
waste beyond the expected level, valued separately and kept out of the cost of good output
the measure of activity that makes a support outlay arise
measuring one result against the best practice found elsewhere
items.s: benchmarking: measuring one result against the best practice found elsewhere. The other options describe cost driver, allocation, abnormal loss.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines passenger journey?
o: a term allowing the agreed sum to rise if input prices increase
goods that have entered a stage but are not yet ready to leave it
the carrying of one traveller over the whole route once
the charging of a whole item of outlay to the section that caused it

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines adverse variance.
o: the record that gathers the input of one stage and shows the output transferred onward
a gap that reduces profit compared with the plan
the pattern in which the hours needed per item fall by a fixed proportion as output doubles
a quantified plan for a defined period, expressed in money or in quantity
items.s: adverse variance: a gap that reduces profit compared with the plan. The other options describe process account, learning curve, budget.

items.q: budget period may be defined as
o: the value of finished stages that the customer surveyor has approved
the effect of paying above or below the planned rate for the quantities purchased
the length of the stretch of activity a plan is drawn to cover
waste beyond the expected level, valued separately and kept out of the cost of good output
items.s: budget period: the length of the stretch of activity a plan is drawn to cover. The other options describe work certified, material price variance, abnormal loss.

items.q: integrated system may be defined as
o: the total sum agreed with the customer for completing the job
a single set of records that serves both the financial and the costing purposes of the firm
the extra outlay caused by making one more item
contribution expressed as a percentage of sales value
items.s: integrated system: a single set of records that serves both the financial and the costing purposes of the firm. The other options describe contract price, marginal cost, profit-volume ratio.

items.q: Which term is described by “apportioning common outlay in the ratio of what each output fetches”?
o: common cost
sales value method
physical units method
joint products

items.q: Which statement correctly defines absorption?
o: a term allowing the agreed sum to rise if input prices increase
contribution expressed as a percentage of sales value
an amount brought into the costing records for something the firm uses but does not pay for
the spreading of indirect outlay over output so that each item carries a share
items.s: absorption: the spreading of indirect outlay over output so that each item carries a share. The other options describe escalation clause, notional charge, profit-volume ratio.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines work in progress.
o: examining what each part of an item does in order to remove needless outlay
goods that have entered a stage but are not yet ready to leave it
the waste that ordinary working conditions make unavoidable in a process
the excess of indirect outlay charged to output above what was actually incurred
items.s: work in progress: goods that have entered a stage but are not yet ready to leave it. The other options describe value analysis, over-absorption, normal loss.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines profit-volume ratio.
o: the planned indirect outlay of a department divided by its planned activity
contribution expressed as a percentage of sales value
a quantified plan for a defined period, expressed in money or in quantity
outlay that arises whether or not the vehicle moves
items.s: profit-volume ratio: contribution expressed as a percentage of sales value. The other options describe budget, standing charge, absorption rate.

items.q: Which term is described by “a plan redrawn at the level of activity actually reached”?
o: flexible budget
budget period
budgetary control
production budget
items.s: flexible budget is a plan redrawn at the level of activity actually reached.

items.q: A plant makes 25000 units a year at a unit cost of N56. The cost reduction committee has set a target of cutting 8 percent from the total cost. What saving is being targeted?
items.s: Saving = units x unit cost x rate/100 = 25000 x 56 x 8/100 = 112000 naira.

items.q: In a process 2000 units were completed and transferred out. Closing work in progress was 600 units, 60 percent complete. What are the equivalent units of output?
items.s: Equivalent units = completed + work in progress x degree of completion = 2000 + 600 x 60/100 = 2360.

items.q: Joint costs of N800000 produced a main product and a by-product. The by-product sells for N40000 and costs N15000 to sell. What joint cost is charged to the main product?
items.s: Joint cost of the main product = 800000 - (40000 - 15000) = 775000 naira.

items.q: The standard price of a material is N30 a unit and 3000 units were bought at N32 each. What is the material price variance, taking a saving as positive and an excess as negative?
items.s: Price variance = (standard - actual) x quantity bought = (30 - 32) x 3000 = -6000 naira.

items.q: The standard wage rate is N150 an hour and 1800 hours were worked, paid at N140 an hour. What is the labour rate variance, taking a saving as positive and an excess as negative?
items.s: Rate variance = (standard rate - actual rate) x hours paid = (150 - 140) x 1800 = 18000 naira.

items.q: Budgeted overhead for a department is N1080000 for 36000 machine hours. In the period 33000 hours were worked. How much overhead was absorbed?
items.s: Absorption rate = 1080000/36000 = 30 per hour; absorbed = 30 x 33000 = 990000 naira.

items.q: The production budget is 4000 units and each unit needs 2 kilograms of material. Opening raw material is 2500 kilograms and closing raw material is 2500 kilograms. What is the purchase budget in kilograms?
items.s: Usage = 4000 x 2 = 8000 kg; purchases = usage + closing - opening = 8000 + 2500 - 2500 = 8000 kg.

items.q: Fixed costs are N480000 and the contribution per unit is N60. What is the break-even point in units?
items.s: Break-even units = fixed cost/contribution per unit = 480000/60 = 8000 units.

items.q: Fixed costs are N600000 and the profit-volume ratio is 40 percent. What is the break-even sales value?
items.s: Break-even sales = fixed cost/(profit-volume ratio/100) = 600000/(40/100) = 1500000 naira.

items.q: Budgeted production overhead is N900000 and budgeted direct labour hours are 30000. What is the overhead absorption rate per direct labour hour?
items.s: Absorption rate = 900000/30000 = 30 naira per hour.

items.q: Rent of N900000 is shared between two departments on floor area. Department A occupies 1800 square metres and department B occupies 600 square metres. What rent is charged to department A?
A bus covers 100000 kilometres in a year. Running cost is N18 a kilometre and the fixed cost for the year is N600000. What is the cost per kilometre?
A division earns a profit of N450000 on assets employed of N3000000. What is the return on investment, as a percentage?
items.s: Return on investment = 450000/3000000 x 100 = 15 percent.

items.q: A branch trades in premises owned by the firm. A notional rent of N360000 a year is charged in the branch records although no money is paid. Before this charge the branch shows a profit of N1150000. What profit is left after it?
items.s: Profit after the notional charge = 1150000 - 360000 = 790000 naira.
items.t: Cost accounting systems and the cost ledger

items.q: A process receives 1000 units. Normal loss is 4 percent of input and each lost unit can be sold for N25. What amount is credited to the process for the expected waste?
items.s: Waste = 1000 x 4/100 = 40 units; scrap credit = 40 x 25 = 1000 naira.

items.q: A process starts with 2000 units at a total cost of N620000. Normal loss is 8 percent of input and the waste sells for N15 a unit. Actual output was 1104 units. What is the value of the abnormal loss?
items.s: Expected good output = 2000 - 160 = 1840 units, cost per good unit = (620000 - 160 x 15)/1840 = 335.65; abnormal loss = (1840 - 1104) x 335.65 = 247040 naira.

items.q: A process receives 4000 units at a total cost of N400000. Normal loss is 5 percent of input and the waste sells for N10 a unit. Actual output was 3952 units. What is the value of the abnormal gain?
items.s: Expected good output = 4000 - 200 = 3800 units, cost per good unit = (400000 - 200 x 10)/3800 = 104.74; abnormal gain = (3952 - 3800) x 104.74 = 15920 naira.

items.q: A process incurs costs of N720000 on 2500 units. Normal loss is 5 percent of input and each lost unit is sold for N20. What is the cost per good unit?
items.s: Good output = 2500 - 125 = 2375 units; net cost = 720000 - 125 x 20 = 717500; cost per good unit = 302.11.

items.q: Joint costs of N1200000 produced 4000 units of product A selling at N60 and 1000 units of product B selling at N120. Using the sales value method, what joint cost is charged to product A?

Joint costs of N640000 were incurred. Product A: 3000 units sell at N120 after further costs of N60000. Product B: 1500 units sell at N140 after further costs of N40000. Under the net realisable value method, what joint cost is charged to product A?
Joint costs of N720000 produced 4000 kilograms of product A and 3000 kilograms of product B. Using the physical units method, what joint cost is charged to product A?
A contract has a price of N6000000. The surveyor has certified 80 percent of the work. What is the value of work certified?
items.s: Value certified = contract price x rate/100 = 6000000 x 80/100 = 4800000 naira.

items.q: Work certified on a contract is N2400000 and the agreement provides for retention of 15 percent. How much is held back?
items.s: Retention = 2400000 x 15/100 = 360000 naira.

items.q: Cost incurred on a contract to date is N3400000, of which N220000 relates to work not yet certified. What is the cost of work certified?
items.s: Cost of work certified = 3400000 - 220000 = 3180000 naira.

items.q: Notional profit on a contract is N660000. Work certified is N2400000 and cash received is N1300000. The firm takes credit for the part of notional profit that cash received bears to work certified. What profit is taken?
Work certified is N3000000 with retention of 10 percent. The customer has already paid N1500000. What amount is still due from the customer?
items.s: Still due = 3000000 - retention (3000000 x 10/100 = 300000) - already paid 1500000 = 1200000 naira.

items.q: The standard input for the output produced is 3600 units at a standard price of N25. Actual input used was 4400 units. What is the material usage variance, taking a saving as positive and an excess as negative?
items.s: Usage variance = (standard quantity - actual quantity) x standard price = (3600 - 4400) x 25 = -20000 naira.

items.q: The standard hours for the output produced are 1800 and 1750 hours were actually worked. The standard rate is N150 an hour. What is the labour efficiency variance, taking a saving as positive and an excess as negative?
items.s: Efficiency variance = (standard hours - actual hours) x standard rate = (1800 - 1750) x 150 = 7500 naira.

items.q: Budgeted overhead is N720000 for 20000 machine hours. Actual hours worked were 21000 and actual overhead incurred was N700000. What is the over or under absorption, taking over absorption as positive and under absorption as negative?
items.s: Absorption rate = 720000/20000 = 36; absorbed = 36 x 21000 = 756000; over or under = 756000 - 700000 = 56000 naira.

items.q: Budgeted sales are 12000 units. Opening finished stock is 600 units and closing finished stock is budgeted at 900 units. What is the production budget in units?
items.s: Production = sales + closing stock - opening stock = 12000 + 900 - 600 = 12300 units.

items.q: A budget provides for 8000 units, each needing 2 direct labour hours at N180 an hour. What is the direct labour budget?
items.s: Labour budget = 8000 x 2 x 180 = 2880000 naira.

items.q: At a budgeted volume of 5000 units the variable cost is N30 a unit and fixed cost is N240000. What total cost should be allowed if 6000 units are actually made?
items.s: Allowed cost = variable x actual units + fixed = 30 x 6000 + 240000 = 420000 naira.

items.q: A product sells for N150 and its variable cost is N110 a unit. What is the contribution per unit?
items.s: Contribution = selling price - variable cost = 150 - 110 = 40 naira.

items.q: Actual sales are N1500000 and break-even sales are N900000. What is the margin of safety as a percentage of actual sales?
items.s: Margin of safety = (1500000 - 900000)/1500000 x 100 = 40 percent.

items.q: Fixed costs are N420000, contribution per unit is N40 and the profit target is N300000. How many units must be sold?
items.s: Units = (fixed cost + target profit)/contribution per unit = (420000 + 300000)/40 = 18000 units.

items.q: Each unit needs 4 hours of a skilled grade. Only 8000 such hours are available and the contribution is N75 a unit. Fixed costs are N90000. What is the greatest profit the firm can make?
items.s: Units possible = 8000/4 = 2000; contribution earned = 2000 x 75 = 150000; profit = 150000 - 90000 = 60000 naira.

items.q: A component can be made in house or bought outside. Making it would need a special machine hired at N210000 and variable costs of N450000. Fixed overhead of N90000 would be incurred either way. What is the relevant cost of making it?
items.s: Relevant cost = avoidable hire + variable cost = 210000 + 450000 = 660000 naira; the fixed overhead is common to both choices.

items.q: A support activity has a cost pool of N450000 and is driven by 1200 setups. Under activity based costing, what is the rate per setup?
items.s: Rate per setup = 450000/1200 = 375 naira.

items.q: A service department's costs of N950000 are apportioned 40 percent to production department A and 40 percent to production department B. What total is charged to the two production departments?
items.s: Charge to production = 950000 x (100 - 40 - 40)/100 = 190000 naira.

items.q: A haulage firm carries 60 tonnes of load over 250 kilometres at a total cost of N600000. What is the cost per tonne-kilometre?
items.s: Tonne-kilometres = 60 x 250 = 15000; cost per unit = 600000/15000 = 40 naira.

items.q: A vehicle has a standing charge of N600000 a year and a running cost of N25 a kilometre. It is expected to cover 20000 kilometres. What is the total operating cost for the year?
items.s: Total cost = standing charge + running cost x distance = 600000 + 25 x 20000 = 1100000 naira.

items.q: A division earns a profit of N750000 on assets of N4000000. The firm charges 10 percent on the assets employed. What is the residual income?
items.s: Residual income = profit - charge = 750000 - (4000000 x 10/100) = 350000 naira.

items.q: The full cost of a component is N120 and the transfer pricing rule is full cost plus 25 percent. What is the transfer price?
items.s: Transfer price = full cost x (100 + mark-up)/100 = 120 x (100 + 25)/100 = 150 naira.

items.q: A product must sell at N240 a unit to remain competitive and the firm requires a margin of 40 percent on selling price. What is the target cost per unit?
items.s: Allowed revenue is the price itself; target cost = 240 x (100 - 40)/100 = 144 naira.

items.q: The cost ledger control account opens with a credit balance of N240000. Costs put through the account during the period were N1200000 and amounts taken out to the financial ledger were N1380000. What is the closing credit balance?
items.s: Closing balance = opening balance + costs put through - amounts taken out = 240000 + 1200000 - 1380000 = 60000 naira.
items.t: Cost accounting systems and the cost ledger

items.q: A plant makes 25000 units a year at a unit cost of N85. The cost reduction committee has set a target of cutting 5 percent from the total cost. What saving is being targeted?
items.s: Saving = units x unit cost x rate/100 = 25000 x 85 x 5/100 = 106250 naira.

items.q: In a process 1600 units were completed and transferred out. Closing work in progress was 400 units, 75 percent complete. What are the equivalent units of output?
items.s: Equivalent units = completed + work in progress x degree of completion = 1600 + 400 x 75/100 = 1900.

items.q: Joint costs of N960000 produced a main product and a by-product. The by-product sells for N60000 and costs N5000 to sell. What joint cost is charged to the main product?
items.s: Joint cost of the main product = 960000 - (60000 - 5000) = 905000 naira.

items.q: The value of work certified on a contract is N2600000 and the cost of that certified work is N1800000. What is the notional profit?
items.s: Notional profit = 2600000 - 1800000 = 800000 naira.

items.q: The standard price of a material is N20 a unit and 3000 units were bought at N32 each. What is the material price variance, taking a saving as positive and an excess as negative?
items.s: Price variance = (standard - actual) x quantity bought = (20 - 32) x 3000 = -36000 naira.

items.q: The standard wage rate is N120 an hour and 2000 hours were worked, paid at N140 an hour. What is the labour rate variance, taking a saving as positive and an excess as negative?
items.s: Rate variance = (standard rate - actual rate) x hours paid = (120 - 140) x 2000 = -40000 naira.

items.q: Budgeted overhead for a department is N1080000 for 36000 machine hours. In the period 26000 hours were worked. How much overhead was absorbed?
items.s: Absorption rate = 1080000/36000 = 30 per hour; absorbed = 30 x 26000 = 780000 naira.

items.q: The production budget is 4000 units and each unit needs 3 kilograms of material. Opening raw material is 2500 kilograms and closing raw material is 3000 kilograms. What is the purchase budget in kilograms?
items.s: Usage = 4000 x 3 = 12000 kg; purchases = usage + closing - opening = 12000 + 3000 - 2500 = 12500 kg.

items.q: The cash budget opens with a balance of N250000. Receipts for the month are N2400000 and payments are N1750000. What is the closing cash balance?
Fixed costs are N480000 and the profit-volume ratio is 50 percent. What is the break-even sales value?
items.s: Break-even sales = fixed cost/(profit-volume ratio/100) = 480000/(50/100) = 960000 naira.

items.q: A bus covers 80000 kilometres in a year. Running cost is N22 a kilometre and the fixed cost for the year is N900000. What is the cost per kilometre?
A division earns a profit of N450000 on assets employed of N4000000. What is the return on investment, as a percentage?
items.s: Return on investment = 450000/4000000 x 100 = 11.25 percent.

items.q: A branch trades in premises owned by the firm. A notional rent of N360000 a year is charged in the branch records although no money is paid. Before this charge the branch shows a profit of N1680000. What profit is left after it?
items.s: Profit after the notional charge = 1680000 - 360000 = 1320000 naira.
items.t: Cost accounting systems and the cost ledger

items.q: A process receives 5000 units. Normal loss is 5 percent of input and each lost unit can be sold for N20. What amount is credited to the process for the expected waste?
items.s: Waste = 5000 x 5/100 = 250 units; scrap credit = 250 x 20 = 5000 naira.

items.q: A process starts with 5000 units at a total cost of N360000. Normal loss is 8 percent of input and the waste sells for N20 a unit. Actual output was 3220 units. What is the value of the abnormal loss?
items.s: Expected good output = 5000 - 400 = 4600 units, cost per good unit = (360000 - 400 x 20)/4600 = 76.52; abnormal loss = (4600 - 3220) x 76.52 = 105600 naira.

items.q: The best definition of margin of safety among these is
o: contribution expressed as a percentage of sales value
the amount by which actual sales exceed those needed to avoid a loss
a future outlay that differs between the choices open to the firm
sales value less the variable outlay of the items sold
items.s: margin of safety: the amount by which actual sales exceed those needed to avoid a loss. The other options describe contribution, profit-volume ratio, relevant cost.

items.q: The statement “the resource in shortest supply that holds back the level of activity” describes which of the following?
o: profit-volume ratio
shut-down point
marginal cost
limiting factor
items.s: limiting factor is the resource in shortest supply that holds back the level of activity.

items.q: The best definition of activity based costing among these is
o: the shortfall of indirect outlay charged to output compared with what was incurred
the sharing of an outlay between sections on a stated basis
charging indirect outlay to items according to the demands each makes on support work
the charging of a whole item of outlay to the section that caused it
items.s: activity based costing: charging indirect outlay to items according to the demands each makes on support work. The other options describe apportionment, under-absorption, allocation.

items.q: standing charge is best described as
o: outlay that varies with the distance covered
the carrying of one traveller over the whole route once
money set aside at intervals to meet the expected cost of repairs
outlay that arises whether or not the vehicle moves
items.s: standing charge: outlay that arises whether or not the vehicle moves. The other options describe passenger journey, maintenance provision, running cost.

items.q: Which term is described by “a gap that reduces profit compared with the plan”?
o: standard cost
idle time variance
adverse variance
material price variance
items.s: adverse variance is a gap that reduces profit compared with the plan.

items.q: Which term is described by “the spreading of indirect outlay over output so that each item carries a share”?
o: under-absorption
apportionment
absorption
cost driver
items.s: absorption is the spreading of indirect outlay over output so that each item carries a share.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “money set aside at intervals to meet the expected cost of repairs”
o: running cost
operating cost statement
maintenance provision
vehicle utilisation
items.s: maintenance provision is money set aside at intervals to meet the expected cost of repairs.

items.q: work in progress is best described as
o: output above the expected level, credited to the process at the same rate as the expected waste
the amount realisable by selling waste material
the waste that ordinary working conditions make unavoidable in a process
goods that have entered a stage but are not yet ready to leave it
items.s: work in progress: goods that have entered a stage but are not yet ready to leave it. The other options describe scrap value, abnormal gain, normal loss.

items.q: The best definition of work certified among these is
o: the outlay on stages finished but not yet approved for payment
the amount actually collected from the customer so far
a term allowing the agreed sum to rise if input prices increase
the value of finished stages that the customer surveyor has approved
items.s: work certified: the value of finished stages that the customer surveyor has approved. The other options describe cash received, escalation clause, work uncertified.

items.q: Choose the option that explains what work certified means.
o: the outlay on the stages that the surveyor has approved
the amount actually collected from the customer so far
the value of finished stages that the customer surveyor has approved
the outlay on stages finished but not yet approved for payment
items.s: work certified: the value of finished stages that the customer surveyor has approved. The other options describe work uncertified, cash received, cost of work certified.

items.q: In this course, shut-down point refers to
o: the level of sales at which keeping going costs more than stopping
a future outlay that differs between the choices open to the firm
the extra outlay caused by making one more item
the resource in shortest supply that holds back the level of activity

items.q: Choose the option that explains what net realisable value method means.

items.q: A process incurs costs of N480000 on 2500 units. Normal loss is 4 percent of input and each lost unit is sold for N20. What is the cost per good unit?
items.s: Good output = 2500 - 100 = 2400 units; net cost = 480000 - 100 x 20 = 478000; cost per good unit = 199.17.

items.q: Joint costs of N1200000 produced 5000 units of product A selling at N90 and 2000 units of product B selling at N100. Using the sales value method, what joint cost is charged to product A?
Joint costs of N720000 produced 6000 kilograms of product A and 3000 kilograms of product B. Using the physical units method, what joint cost is charged to product A?
Cost incurred on a contract to date is N1650000, of which N120000 relates to work not yet certified. What is the cost of work certified?
items.s: Cost of work certified = 1650000 - 120000 = 1530000 naira.

items.q: The standard input for the output produced is 4800 units at a standard price of N20. Actual input used was 5000 units. What is the material usage variance, taking a saving as positive and an excess as negative?
items.s: Usage variance = (standard quantity - actual quantity) x standard price = (4800 - 5000) x 20 = -4000 naira.

items.q: The standard hours for the output produced are 1600 and 1250 hours were actually worked. The standard rate is N100 an hour. What is the labour efficiency variance, taking a saving as positive and an excess as negative?
items.s: Efficiency variance = (standard hours - actual hours) x standard rate = (1600 - 1250) x 100 = 35000 naira.

items.q: At a budgeted volume of 5000 units the variable cost is N30 a unit and fixed cost is N240000. What total cost should be allowed if 7000 units are actually made?
items.s: Allowed cost = variable x actual units + fixed = 30 x 7000 + 240000 = 450000 naira.

items.q: Fixed costs are N600000, contribution per unit is N40 and the profit target is N300000. How many units must be sold?
items.s: Units = (fixed cost + target profit)/contribution per unit = (600000 + 300000)/40 = 22500 units.

items.q: A support activity has a cost pool of N600000 and is driven by 900 setups. Under activity based costing, what is the rate per setup?
items.s: Rate per setup = 600000/900 = 666.67 naira.

items.q: A haulage firm carries 50 tonnes of load over 250 kilometres at a total cost of N600000. What is the cost per tonne-kilometre?
items.s: Tonne-kilometres = 50 x 250 = 12500; cost per unit = 600000/12500 = 48 naira.

items.q: A division earns a profit of N600000 on assets of N3000000. The firm charges 8 percent on the assets employed. What is the residual income?
items.s: Residual income = profit - charge = 600000 - (3000000 x 8/100) = 360000 naira.

items.q: A plant makes 18000 units a year at a unit cost of N85. The cost reduction committee has set a target of cutting 4 percent from the total cost. What saving is being targeted?
items.s: Saving = units x unit cost x rate/100 = 18000 x 85 x 4/100 = 61200 naira.

items.q: A process receives 2000 units. Normal loss is 12 percent of input and each lost unit can be sold for N20. What amount is credited to the process for the expected waste?
items.s: Waste = 2000 x 12/100 = 240 units; scrap credit = 240 x 20 = 4800 naira.

items.q: A process starts with 4000 units at a total cost of N480000. Normal loss is 10 percent of input and the waste sells for N10 a unit. Actual output was 2880 units. What is the value of the abnormal loss?
items.s: Expected good output = 4000 - 400 = 3600 units, cost per good unit = (480000 - 400 x 10)/3600 = 132.22; abnormal loss = (3600 - 2880) x 132.22 = 95200 naira.

items.q: A process receives 3000 units at a total cost of N780000. Normal loss is 10 percent of input and the waste sells for N10 a unit. Actual output was 2754 units. What is the value of the abnormal gain?
items.s: Expected good output = 3000 - 300 = 2700 units, cost per good unit = (780000 - 300 x 10)/2700 = 287.78; abnormal gain = (2754 - 2700) x 287.78 = 15540 naira.

items.q: In a process 1600 units were completed and transferred out. Closing work in progress was 400 units, 25 percent complete. What are the equivalent units of output?
items.s: Equivalent units = completed + work in progress x degree of completion = 1600 + 400 x 25/100 = 1700.

items.q: Joint costs of N640000 were incurred. Product A: 2000 units sell at N100 after further costs of N40000. Product B: 1500 units sell at N140 after further costs of N50000. Under the net realisable value method, what joint cost is charged to product A?
Joint costs of N960000 produced a main product and a by-product. The by-product sells for N90000 and costs N10000 to sell. What joint cost is charged to the main product?
items.s: Joint cost of the main product = 960000 - (90000 - 10000) = 880000 naira.

items.q: Work certified on a contract is N3000000 and the agreement provides for retention of 5 percent. How much is held back?
items.s: Retention = 3000000 x 5/100 = 150000 naira.

items.q: Work certified is N2600000 and retention is 10 percent. The customer has paid everything except the retention. What cash has been received?

Notional profit on a contract is N300000. Work certified is N3000000 and cash received is N1700000. The firm takes credit for the part of notional profit that cash received bears to work certified. What profit is taken?
Work certified is N3000000 with retention of 5 percent. The customer has already paid N900000. What amount is still due from the customer?
items.s: Still due = 3000000 - retention (3000000 x 5/100 = 150000) - already paid 900000 = 1950000 naira.

items.q: The standard price of a material is N40 a unit and 5000 units were bought at N22 each. What is the material price variance, taking a saving as positive and an excess as negative?
items.s: Price variance = (standard - actual) x quantity bought = (40 - 22) x 5000 = 90000 naira.

items.q: The standard wage rate is N100 an hour and 1500 hours were worked, paid at N140 an hour. What is the labour rate variance, taking a saving as positive and an excess as negative?
items.s: Rate variance = (standard rate - actual rate) x hours paid = (100 - 140) x 1500 = -60000 naira.

items.q: Budgeted overhead is N720000 for 20000 machine hours. Actual hours worked were 33000 and actual overhead incurred was N700000. What is the over or under absorption, taking over absorption as positive and under absorption as negative?
items.s: Absorption rate = 720000/20000 = 36; absorbed = 36 x 33000 = 1188000; over or under = 1188000 - 700000 = 488000 naira.

items.q: Budgeted sales are 12000 units. Opening finished stock is 600 units and closing finished stock is budgeted at 1200 units. What is the production budget in units?
items.s: Production = sales + closing stock - opening stock = 12000 + 1200 - 600 = 12600 units.

items.q: The production budget is 7500 units and each unit needs 2 kilograms of material. Opening raw material is 2500 kilograms and closing raw material is 2500 kilograms. What is the purchase budget in kilograms?
items.s: Usage = 7500 x 2 = 15000 kg; purchases = usage + closing - opening = 15000 + 2500 - 2500 = 15000 kg.

items.q: The cash budget opens with a balance of N250000. Receipts for the month are N1800000 and payments are N1950000. What is the closing cash balance?
Fixed costs are N480000 and the profit-volume ratio is 60 percent. What is the break-even sales value?
items.s: Break-even sales = fixed cost/(profit-volume ratio/100) = 480000/(60/100) = 800000 naira.

items.q: Budgeted production overhead is N600000 and budgeted direct labour hours are 30000. What is the overhead absorption rate per direct labour hour?
items.s: Absorption rate = 600000/30000 = 20 naira per hour.

items.q: Rent of N900000 is shared between two departments on floor area. Department A occupies 1500 square metres and department B occupies 600 square metres. What rent is charged to department A?
A service department's costs of N950000 are apportioned 50 percent to production department A and 20 percent to production department B. What total is charged to the two production departments?
items.s: Charge to production = 950000 x (100 - 50 - 20)/100 = 285000 naira.

items.q: A bus covers 150000 kilometres in a year. Running cost is N18 a kilometre and the fixed cost for the year is N720000. What is the cost per kilometre?
The full cost of a component is N80 and the transfer pricing rule is full cost plus 15 percent. What is the transfer price?
items.s: Transfer price = full cost x (100 + mark-up)/100 = 80 x (100 + 15)/100 = 92 naira.

items.q: A product must sell at N450 a unit to remain competitive and the firm requires a margin of 20 percent on selling price. What is the target cost per unit?
items.s: Allowed revenue is the price itself; target cost = 450 x (100 - 20)/100 = 360 naira.

items.s: Good output = 5000 - 500 = 4500 units; net cost = 600000 - 500 x 20 = 590000; cost per good unit = 131.11.

items.q: Joint costs of N900000 produced 4000 units of product A selling at N80 and 1000 units of product B selling at N100. Using the sales value method, what joint cost is charged to product A?

The standard input for the output produced is 4200 units at a standard price of N30. Actual input used was 5000 units. What is the material usage variance, taking a saving as positive and an excess as negative?
items.s: Usage variance = (standard quantity - actual quantity) x standard price = (4200 - 5000) x 30 = -24000 naira.

items.q: At a budgeted volume of 5000 units the variable cost is N40 a unit and fixed cost is N240000. What total cost should be allowed if 6000 units are actually made?
items.s: Allowed cost = variable x actual units + fixed = 40 x 6000 + 240000 = 480000 naira.

items.q: Fixed costs are N600000, contribution per unit is N60 and the profit target is N240000. How many units must be sold?
items.s: Units = (fixed cost + target profit)/contribution per unit = (600000 + 240000)/60 = 14000 units.

items.q: A component can be made in house or bought outside. Making it would need a special machine hired at N150000 and variable costs of N380000. Fixed overhead of N120000 would be incurred either way. What is the relevant cost of making it?
items.s: Relevant cost = avoidable hire + variable cost = 150000 + 380000 = 530000 naira; the fixed overhead is common to both choices.

items.q: A support activity has a cost pool of N450000 and is driven by 1500 setups. Under activity based costing, what is the rate per setup?
items.s: Rate per setup = 450000/1500 = 300 naira.

items.q: A haulage firm carries 60 tonnes of load over 250 kilometres at a total cost of N480000. What is the cost per tonne-kilometre?
items.s: Tonne-kilometres = 60 x 250 = 15000; cost per unit = 480000/15000 = 32 naira.

items.q: A plant makes 18000 units a year at a unit cost of N72. The cost reduction committee has set a target of cutting 8 percent from the total cost. What saving is being targeted?
items.s: Saving = units x unit cost x rate/100 = 18000 x 72 x 8/100 = 103680 naira.

items.q: A process receives 2500 units. Normal loss is 5 percent of input and each lost unit can be sold for N25. What amount is credited to the process for the expected waste?
items.s: Waste = 2500 x 5/100 = 125 units; scrap credit = 125 x 25 = 3125 naira.

items.q: A process starts with 3000 units at a total cost of N750000. Normal loss is 8 percent of input and the waste sells for N20 a unit. Actual output was 1656 units. What is the value of the abnormal loss?
items.s: Expected good output = 3000 - 240 = 2760 units, cost per good unit = (750000 - 240 x 20)/2760 = 270; abnormal loss = (2760 - 1656) x 270 = 298080 naira.

items.q: A process receives 3000 units at a total cost of N520000. Normal loss is 10 percent of input and the waste sells for N20 a unit. Actual output was 2754 units. What is the value of the abnormal gain?
items.s: Expected good output = 3000 - 300 = 2700 units, cost per good unit = (520000 - 300 x 20)/2700 = 190.37; abnormal gain = (2754 - 2700) x 190.37 = 10280 naira.

items.q: In a process 1200 units were completed and transferred out. Closing work in progress was 600 units, 60 percent complete. What are the equivalent units of output?
items.s: Equivalent units = completed + work in progress x degree of completion = 1200 + 600 x 60/100 = 1560.

items.q: Joint costs of N500000 were incurred. Product A: 3000 units sell at N100 after further costs of N60000. Product B: 2500 units sell at N140 after further costs of N30000. Under the net realisable value method, what joint cost is charged to product A?
Joint costs of N1150000 produced a main product and a by-product. The by-product sells for N40000 and costs N10000 to sell. What joint cost is charged to the main product?
items.s: Joint cost of the main product = 1150000 - (40000 - 10000) = 1120000 naira.

items.q: A contract has a price of N7500000. The surveyor has certified 40 percent of the work. What is the value of work certified?
items.s: Value certified = contract price x rate/100 = 7500000 x 40/100 = 3000000 naira.

items.q: Work certified is N2600000 and retention is 5 percent. The customer has paid everything except the retention. What cash has been received?
The value of work certified on a contract is N3200000 and the cost of that certified work is N2300000. What is the notional profit?
items.s: Notional profit = 3200000 - 2300000 = 900000 naira.

items.q: Notional profit on a contract is N420000. Work certified is N3000000 and cash received is N2100000. The firm takes credit for the part of notional profit that cash received bears to work certified. What profit is taken?
Work certified is N3000000 with retention of 5 percent. The customer has already paid N1500000. What amount is still due from the customer?
items.s: Still due = 3000000 - retention (3000000 x 5/100 = 150000) - already paid 1500000 = 1350000 naira.

items.q: The standard price of a material is N30 a unit and 4000 units were bought at N36 each. What is the material price variance, taking a saving as positive and an excess as negative?
items.s: Price variance = (standard - actual) x quantity bought = (30 - 36) x 4000 = -24000 naira.

items.q: The standard wage rate is N100 an hour and 1800 hours were worked, paid at N125 an hour. What is the labour rate variance, taking a saving as positive and an excess as negative?
items.s: Rate variance = (standard rate - actual rate) x hours paid = (100 - 125) x 1800 = -45000 naira.

items.q: Budgeted overhead for a department is N1080000 for 24000 machine hours. In the period 26000 hours were worked. How much overhead was absorbed?
items.s: Absorption rate = 1080000/24000 = 45 per hour; absorbed = 45 x 26000 = 1170000 naira.

items.q: Budgeted overhead is N900000 for 24000 machine hours. Actual hours worked were 33000 and actual overhead incurred was N610000. What is the over or under absorption, taking over absorption as positive and under absorption as negative?
Budgeted sales are 15000 units. Opening finished stock is 1000 units and closing finished stock is budgeted at 1200 units. What is the production budget in units?
items.s: Production = sales + closing stock - opening stock = 15000 + 1200 - 1000 = 15200 units.

the pattern in which the hours needed per item fall by a fixed proportion as output doubles
