apportioning common outlay in the ratio of what each output fetches
the stage at which a common input becomes separate identifiable outputs
outlay incurred before the outputs become separately identifiable and shared by them all

items.q: A process receives 5000 units at a total cost of N640000. Normal loss is 12 percent of input and the waste sells for N20 a unit. Actual output was 4576 units. What is the value of the abnormal gain?
items.s: Expected good output = 5000 - 600 = 4400 units, cost per good unit = (640000 - 600 x 20)/4400 = 142.73; abnormal gain = (4576 - 4400) x 142.73 = 25120 naira.

items.q: Joint costs of N800000 were incurred. Product A: 3000 units sell at N100 after further costs of N60000. Product B: 1500 units sell at N150 after further costs of N40000. Under the net realisable value method, what joint cost is charged to product A?

Notional profit on a contract is N540000. Work certified is N3000000 and cash received is N2100000. The firm takes credit for the part of notional profit that cash received bears to work certified. What profit is taken?
Work certified is N3000000 with retention of 10 percent. The customer has already paid N1200000. What amount is still due from the customer?
items.s: Still due = 3000000 - retention (3000000 x 10/100 = 300000) - already paid 1200000 = 1500000 naira.

items.q: Budgeted overhead is N600000 for 20000 machine hours. Actual hours worked were 21000 and actual overhead incurred was N610000. What is the over or under absorption, taking over absorption as positive and under absorption as negative?
items.s: Absorption rate = 600000/20000 = 30; absorbed = 30 x 21000 = 630000; over or under = 630000 - 610000 = 20000 naira.

items.q: A service department's costs of N1100000 are apportioned 40 percent to production department A and 20 percent to production department B. What total is charged to the two production departments?
items.s: Charge to production = 1100000 x (100 - 40 - 20)/100 = 440000 naira.

items.q: A branch trades in premises owned by the firm. A notional rent of N240000 a year is charged in the branch records although no money is paid. Before this charge the branch shows a profit of N1150000. What profit is left after it?
items.s: Profit after the notional charge = 1150000 - 240000 = 910000 naira.
items.t: Cost accounting systems and the cost ledger

items.q: A plant makes 25000 units a year at a unit cost of N85. The cost reduction committee has set a target of cutting 8 percent from the total cost. What saving is being targeted?
items.s: Saving = units x unit cost x rate/100 = 25000 x 85 x 8/100 = 170000 naira.

items.q: A process receives 4000 units. Normal loss is 8 percent of input and each lost unit can be sold for N15. What amount is credited to the process for the expected waste?
items.s: Waste = 4000 x 8/100 = 320 units; scrap credit = 320 x 15 = 4800 naira.

items.q: In a process 2400 units were completed and transferred out. Closing work in progress was 300 units, 25 percent complete. What are the equivalent units of output?
items.s: Equivalent units = completed + work in progress x degree of completion = 2400 + 300 x 25/100 = 2475.

items.q: A process incurs costs of N900000 on 5000 units. Normal loss is 10 percent of input and each lost unit is sold for N20. What is the cost per good unit?
items.s: Good output = 5000 - 500 = 4500 units; net cost = 900000 - 500 x 20 = 890000; cost per good unit = 197.78.

items.q: Joint costs of N600000 produced 3000 units of product A selling at N80 and 1000 units of product B selling at N120. Using the sales value method, what joint cost is charged to product A?
Joint costs of N800000 produced a main product and a by-product. The by-product sells for N60000 and costs N5000 to sell. What joint cost is charged to the main product?
items.s: Joint cost of the main product = 800000 - (60000 - 5000) = 745000 naira.

items.q: Joint costs of N560000 produced 6000 kilograms of product A and 3000 kilograms of product B. Using the physical units method, what joint cost is charged to product A?
A contract has a price of N4500000. The surveyor has certified 30 percent of the work. What is the value of work certified?
items.s: Value certified = contract price x rate/100 = 4500000 x 30/100 = 1350000 naira.

items.q: Work certified on a contract is N3000000 and the agreement provides for retention of 15 percent. How much is held back?
items.s: Retention = 3000000 x 15/100 = 450000 naira.

items.q: Cost incurred on a contract to date is N1650000, of which N150000 relates to work not yet certified. What is the cost of work certified?
items.s: Cost of work certified = 1650000 - 150000 = 1500000 naira.

items.q: The standard price of a material is N20 a unit and 4000 units were bought at N36 each. What is the material price variance, taking a saving as positive and an excess as negative?
items.s: Price variance = (standard - actual) x quantity bought = (20 - 36) x 4000 = -64000 naira.

items.q: The standard input for the output produced is 3800 units at a standard price of N25. Actual input used was 4400 units. What is the material usage variance, taking a saving as positive and an excess as negative?
items.s: Usage variance = (standard quantity - actual quantity) x standard price = (3800 - 4400) x 25 = -15000 naira.

items.q: The standard wage rate is N150 an hour and 1200 hours were worked, paid at N125 an hour. What is the labour rate variance, taking a saving as positive and an excess as negative?
items.s: Rate variance = (standard rate - actual rate) x hours paid = (150 - 125) x 1200 = 30000 naira.

items.q: The standard hours for the output produced are 1800 and 1250 hours were actually worked. The standard rate is N120 an hour. What is the labour efficiency variance, taking a saving as positive and an excess as negative?
items.s: Efficiency variance = (standard hours - actual hours) x standard rate = (1800 - 1250) x 120 = 66000 naira.

items.q: Budgeted overhead for a department is N900000 for 30000 machine hours. In the period 33000 hours were worked. How much overhead was absorbed?
items.s: Absorption rate = 900000/30000 = 30 per hour; absorbed = 30 x 33000 = 990000 naira.

items.q: Budgeted sales are 8000 units. Opening finished stock is 800 units and closing finished stock is budgeted at 1500 units. What is the production budget in units?
items.s: Production = sales + closing stock - opening stock = 8000 + 1500 - 800 = 8700 units.

items.q: The production budget is 6000 units and each unit needs 3 kilograms of material. Opening raw material is 2000 kilograms and closing raw material is 1500 kilograms. What is the purchase budget in kilograms?
items.s: Usage = 6000 x 3 = 18000 kg; purchases = usage + closing - opening = 18000 + 1500 - 2000 = 17500 kg.

items.q: A budget provides for 9000 units, each needing 2 direct labour hours at N120 an hour. What is the direct labour budget?
items.s: Labour budget = 9000 x 2 x 120 = 2160000 naira.

items.q: The cash budget opens with a balance of N250000. Receipts for the month are N2100000 and payments are N1750000. What is the closing cash balance?
At a budgeted volume of 5000 units the variable cost is N30 a unit and fixed cost is N300000. What total cost should be allowed if 6000 units are actually made?
items.s: Allowed cost = variable x actual units + fixed = 30 x 6000 + 300000 = 480000 naira.

items.q: A product sells for N150 and its variable cost is N70 a unit. What is the contribution per unit?
items.s: Contribution = selling price - variable cost = 150 - 70 = 80 naira.

items.q: Fixed costs are N660000 and the contribution per unit is N120. What is the break-even point in units?
items.s: Break-even units = fixed cost/contribution per unit = 660000/120 = 5500 units.

items.q: Fixed costs are N480000, contribution per unit is N60 and the profit target is N300000. How many units must be sold?
items.s: Units = (fixed cost + target profit)/contribution per unit = (480000 + 300000)/60 = 13000 units.

items.q: Budgeted production overhead is N720000 and budgeted direct labour hours are 16000. What is the overhead absorption rate per direct labour hour?
items.s: Absorption rate = 720000/16000 = 45 naira per hour.

items.q: Rent of N750000 is shared between two departments on floor area. Department A occupies 1200 square metres and department B occupies 1000 square metres. What rent is charged to department A?
A bus covers 150000 kilometres in a year. Running cost is N25 a kilometre and the fixed cost for the year is N600000. What is the cost per kilometre?
A haulage firm carries 40 tonnes of load over 400 kilometres at a total cost of N720000. What is the cost per tonne-kilometre?
items.s: Tonne-kilometres = 40 x 400 = 16000; cost per unit = 720000/16000 = 45 naira.

items.q: A vehicle has a standing charge of N600000 a year and a running cost of N20 a kilometre. It is expected to cover 25000 kilometres. What is the total operating cost for the year?
items.s: Total cost = standing charge + running cost x distance = 600000 + 20 x 25000 = 1100000 naira.

items.q: A division earns a profit of N360000 on assets employed of N2400000. What is the return on investment, as a percentage?
items.s: Return on investment = 360000/2400000 x 100 = 15 percent.

items.q: The full cost of a component is N150 and the transfer pricing rule is full cost plus 20 percent. What is the transfer price?
items.s: Transfer price = full cost x (100 + mark-up)/100 = 150 x (100 + 20)/100 = 180 naira.

items.q: A process starts with 4000 units at a total cost of N360000. Normal loss is 5 percent of input and the waste sells for N20 a unit. Actual output was 2660 units. What is the value of the abnormal loss?
items.s: Expected good output = 4000 - 200 = 3800 units, cost per good unit = (360000 - 200 x 20)/3800 = 93.68; abnormal loss = (3800 - 2660) x 93.68 = 106800 naira.

items.q: A process receives 3000 units at a total cost of N520000. Normal loss is 12 percent of input and the waste sells for N10 a unit. Actual output was 2746 units. What is the value of the abnormal gain?

items.q: A service department's costs of N950000 are apportioned 30 percent to production department A and 40 percent to production department B. What total is charged to the two production departments?
items.s: Charge to production = 950000 x (100 - 30 - 40)/100 = 285000 naira.

items.q: A product must sell at N450 a unit to remain competitive and the firm requires a margin of 25 percent on selling price. What is the target cost per unit?
items.s: Allowed revenue is the price itself; target cost = 450 x (100 - 25)/100 = 337.5 naira.

items.q: The cost ledger control account opens with a credit balance of N240000. Costs put through the account during the period were N1450000 and amounts taken out to the financial ledger were N1380000. What is the closing credit balance?
items.s: Closing balance = opening balance + costs put through - amounts taken out = 240000 + 1450000 - 1380000 = 310000 naira.

items.q: The standard input for the output produced is 4800 units at a standard price of N40. Actual input used was 3400 units. What is the material usage variance, taking a saving as positive and an excess as negative?
items.s: Usage variance = (standard quantity - actual quantity) x standard price = (4800 - 3400) x 40 = 56000 naira.

items.q: The standard wage rate is N120 an hour and 1800 hours were worked, paid at N110 an hour. What is the labour rate variance, taking a saving as positive and an excess as negative?
items.s: Rate variance = (standard rate - actual rate) x hours paid = (120 - 110) x 1800 = 18000 naira.

adverse variance
labour efficiency variance
variance

items.q: The correct meaning of benchmarking is
o: setting the allowable outlay by deducting the wanted profit from the price the market will pay
gathering all outlay on an item from design through to withdrawal from use
measuring one result against the best practice found elsewhere
the pattern in which the hours needed per item fall by a fixed proportion as output doubles

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains relevant cost.
o: the resource in shortest supply that holds back the level of activity
contribution expressed as a percentage of sales value
sales value less the variable outlay of the items sold
a future outlay that differs between the choices open to the firm
items.s: relevant cost: a future outlay that differs between the choices open to the firm. The other options describe limiting factor, contribution, profit-volume ratio.

items.q: running cost may be defined as
o: outlay that varies with the distance covered
a measure that combines two things, such as weight carried and distance covered
outlay that arises whether or not the vehicle moves
the proportion of the carrying capacity actually used
items.s: running cost: outlay that varies with the distance covered. The other options describe standing charge, composite cost unit, vehicle utilisation.

items.q: “a quantified plan for a defined period, expressed in money or in quantity” is the definition of
o: budgetary control
budget
production budget
cash budget
items.s: budget is a quantified plan for a defined period, expressed in money or in quantity.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the excess of indirect outlay charged to output above what was actually incurred”
o: over-absorption
apportionment
under-absorption
absorption rate
items.s: over-absorption is the excess of indirect outlay charged to output above what was actually incurred.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains sales value method.

the stage at which a common input becomes separate identifiable outputs
two or more items of similar importance that emerge together from the same raw material
spending incurred after the outputs have become distinct and traceable to one of them

items.q: Which statement correctly defines activity based costing?

the shortfall of indirect outlay charged to output compared with what was incurred
the spreading of indirect outlay over output so that each item carries a share
the charging of a whole item of outlay to the section that caused it

items.q: The correct meaning of learning curve is
o: the pattern in which the hours needed per item fall by a fixed proportion as output doubles
keeping spending within the limits already set for it
examining what each part of an item does in order to remove needless outlay
setting the allowable outlay by deducting the wanted profit from the price the market will pay
items.s: learning curve: the pattern in which the hours needed per item fall by a fixed proportion as output doubles. The other options describe target costing, value analysis, cost control.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains cost control.
o: examining what each part of an item does in order to remove needless outlay
keeping spending within the limits already set for it
measuring one result against the best practice found elsewhere
gathering all outlay on an item from design through to withdrawal from use
items.s: cost control: keeping spending within the limits already set for it. The other options describe benchmarking, life cycle costing, value analysis.

items.q: The correct meaning of feedforward control is
o: a single set of records that serves both the financial and the costing purposes of the firm
an amount brought into the costing records for something the firm uses but does not pay for
corrective action taken on expected future results before those results occur
a schedule that explains why two sets of records show different results for one period

items.q: “two or more items of similar importance that emerge together from the same raw material” is the definition of

a measure that combines two things, such as weight carried and distance covered
a schedule that gathers the fixed and variable outlay of a fleet for a period
the proportion of the carrying capacity actually used
items.s: vehicle utilisation: the proportion of the carrying capacity actually used. The other options describe composite cost unit, standing charge, operating cost statement.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains cash received.

the amount actually collected from the customer so far
the outlay on stages finished but not yet approved for payment

the outlay on stages finished but not yet approved for payment
the total sum agreed with the customer for completing the job

the outlay on the stages that the surveyor has approved
a term allowing the agreed sum to rise if input prices increase
the amount actually collected from the customer so far
items.s: notional profit: the excess of the approved value over the outlay on the stages approved. The other options describe escalation clause, cash received, cost of work certified.

o: the rate at which a plant turns input into saleable output
a real saving in the outlay of a unit without loss of quality
the pattern in which the hours needed per item fall by a fixed proportion as output doubles
examining what each part of an item does in order to remove needless outlay
items.s: cost reduction: a real saving in the outlay of a unit without loss of quality. The other options describe value analysis, learning curve, throughput.

o: corrective action taken on expected future results before those results occur
a working paper that spreads indirect outlay across the sections of a factory
a schedule that explains why two sets of records show different results for one period
a single set of records that serves both the financial and the costing purposes of the firm

throughput
life cycle costing
cost reduction

the extra outlay caused by making one more item
a future outlay that differs between the choices open to the firm
the amount by which actual sales exceed those needed to avoid a loss
items.s: relevant cost: a future outlay that differs between the choices open to the firm. The other options describe marginal cost, margin of safety, limiting factor.

the record that gathers the input of one stage and shows the output transferred onward
the waste that ordinary working conditions make unavoidable in a process
output above the expected level, credited to the process at the same rate as the expected waste

a measure that converts partly finished work into the number of complete items it equals
the amount realisable by selling waste material

keeping spending within the limits already set for it

maintenance provision
service costing

spending incurred after the outputs have become distinct and traceable to one of them

o: cost reduction

work in progress

the charging of a whole item of outlay to the section that caused it
charging indirect outlay to items according to the demands each makes on support work
the excess of indirect outlay charged to output above what was actually incurred

o: cost of work certified

contract price

the outlay on the stages that the surveyor has approved
the value of finished stages that the customer surveyor has approved
items.s: work uncertified: the outlay on stages finished but not yet approved for payment. The other options describe cost of work certified, work certified, contract price.

items.q: In this course, zero-based budgeting refers to
o: the quantity to be made, worked out from sales and the opening and closing holdings
the setting of plans, the comparison of actual with plan, and action on the differences
building every plan from nothing so that each item must be justified afresh
a plan redrawn at the level of activity actually reached
items.s: zero-based budgeting: building every plan from nothing so that each item must be justified afresh. The other options describe budgetary control, production budget, flexible budget.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines separable cost?
o: two or more items of similar importance that emerge together from the same raw material
apportioning on selling price less the further spending needed to complete and sell
a minor item emerging alongside the main output and small in value compared with it
spending incurred after the outputs have become distinct and traceable to one of them
items.s: separable cost: spending incurred after the outputs have become distinct and traceable to one of them. The other options describe joint products, by-product, net realisable value method.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “gathering all outlay on an item from design through to withdrawal from use”
o: learning curve
cost reduction
life cycle costing
cost control
items.s: life cycle costing is gathering all outlay on an item from design through to withdrawal from use.

items.q: material price variance may be defined as
o: the planned outlay for one item, built up from technical specifications
a gap that increases profit compared with the plan
the effect of paying above or below the planned rate for the quantities purchased
the charge for paid hours in which no output was produced, always adverse
items.s: material price variance: the effect of paying above or below the planned rate for the quantities purchased. The other options describe standard cost, favourable variance, idle time variance.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “measuring one result against the best practice found elsewhere”
o: life cycle costing
throughput
benchmarking
value analysis
items.s: benchmarking is measuring one result against the best practice found elsewhere.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines abnormal loss?
o: waste beyond the expected level, valued separately and kept out of the cost of good output
goods that have entered a stage but are not yet ready to leave it
the record that gathers the input of one stage and shows the output transferred onward
the amount realisable by selling waste material
items.s: abnormal loss: waste beyond the expected level, valued separately and kept out of the cost of good output. The other options describe process account, scrap value, work in progress.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains escalation clause.
o: the amount actually collected from the customer so far
the total sum agreed with the customer for completing the job
the value of finished stages that the customer surveyor has approved
a term allowing the agreed sum to rise if input prices increase
items.s: escalation clause: a term allowing the agreed sum to rise if input prices increase. The other options describe work certified, cash received, contract price.

items.q: “the sharing of an outlay between sections on a stated basis” is the definition of
o: absorption
allocation
apportionment
absorption rate
items.s: apportionment is the sharing of an outlay between sections on a stated basis.

items.q: The correct meaning of sales value method is
o: the stage at which a common input becomes separate identifiable outputs
outlay incurred before the outputs become separately identifiable and shared by them all
apportioning common outlay in the ratio of what each output fetches
spending incurred after the outputs have become distinct and traceable to one of them
items.s: sales value method: apportioning common outlay in the ratio of what each output fetches. The other options describe separable cost, split-off point, common cost.

items.q: In this course, process account refers to
o: the waste that ordinary working conditions make unavoidable in a process
the proportion of the processing on partly finished items that has already been carried out
goods that have entered a stage but are not yet ready to leave it
the record that gathers the input of one stage and shows the output transferred onward
items.s: process account: the record that gathers the input of one stage and shows the output transferred onward. The other options describe normal loss, work in progress, degree of completion.

items.q: The correct meaning of margin of safety is
o: contribution expressed as a percentage of sales value
sales value less the variable outlay of the items sold
the level of sales at which keeping going costs more than stopping
the amount by which actual sales exceed those needed to avoid a loss
items.s: margin of safety: the amount by which actual sales exceed those needed to avoid a loss. The other options describe contribution, profit-volume ratio, shut-down point.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines favourable variance?
o: the effect of using more or less input than the recipe allows, valued at the planned rate
the gap between a planned figure and the figure actually recorded
a gap that increases profit compared with the plan
the effect of working faster or slower than the planned hours for the output produced
items.s: favourable variance: a gap that increases profit compared with the plan. The other options describe material usage variance, labour efficiency variance, variance.

items.q: “the gap between a planned figure and the figure actually recorded” is the definition of
o: adverse variance
standard cost
variance
favourable variance
items.s: variance is the gap between a planned figure and the figure actually recorded.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the extra outlay caused by making one more item”
o: marginal cost
relevant cost
profit-volume ratio
break-even point
items.s: marginal cost is the extra outlay caused by making one more item.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains cash budget.
o: the length of the stretch of activity a plan is drawn to cover
the quantity to be made, worked out from sales and the opening and closing holdings
a forecast of money coming in and going out and of the balance left
a quantified plan for a defined period, expressed in money or in quantity
items.s: cash budget: a forecast of money coming in and going out and of the balance left. The other options describe budget period, production budget, budget.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines absorption rate?
o: the planned indirect outlay of a department divided by its planned activity
the measure of activity that makes a support outlay arise
the shortfall of indirect outlay charged to output compared with what was incurred
the excess of indirect outlay charged to output above what was actually incurred
items.s: absorption rate: the planned indirect outlay of a department divided by its planned activity. The other options describe cost driver, over-absorption, under-absorption.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains integrated system.
o: the use of common methods and terms by several firms within one industry
a single set of records that serves both the financial and the costing purposes of the firm
corrective action taken on expected future results before those results occur
a working paper that spreads indirect outlay across the sections of a factory
items.s: integrated system: a single set of records that serves both the financial and the costing purposes of the firm. The other options describe uniform costing, cost apportionment sheet, feedforward control.
items.t: Cost accounting systems and the cost ledger

items.q: “the charge for paid hours in which no output was produced, always adverse” is the definition of
o: adverse variance
idle time variance
standard cost
favourable variance
items.s: idle time variance is the charge for paid hours in which no output was produced, always adverse.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains labour efficiency variance.
o: the effect of using more or less input than the recipe allows, valued at the planned rate
the charge for paid hours in which no output was produced, always adverse
the planned outlay for one item, built up from technical specifications
the effect of working faster or slower than the planned hours for the output produced
items.s: labour efficiency variance: the effect of working faster or slower than the planned hours for the output produced. The other options describe standard cost, material usage variance, idle time variance.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “a single set of records that serves both the financial and the costing purposes of the firm”
o: cost apportionment sheet
reconciliation statement
uniform costing
integrated system
items.s: integrated system is a single set of records that serves both the financial and the costing purposes of the firm.
items.t: Cost accounting systems and the cost ledger

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains reconciliation statement.
o: corrective action taken on expected future results before those results occur
a schedule that explains why two sets of records show different results for one period
the use of common methods and terms by several firms within one industry
a single set of records that serves both the financial and the costing purposes of the firm
items.s: reconciliation statement: a schedule that explains why two sets of records show different results for one period. The other options describe feedforward control, uniform costing, integrated system.
items.t: Cost accounting systems and the cost ledger

items.q: The correct meaning of purchase budget is
o: the quantity to be made, worked out from sales and the opening and closing holdings
a quantified plan for a defined period, expressed in money or in quantity
the quantity of input to be bought, from the usage and the change in holdings
a plan redrawn at the level of activity actually reached
items.s: purchase budget: the quantity of input to be bought, from the usage and the change in holdings. The other options describe flexible budget, production budget, budget.

items.q: “the setting of plans, the comparison of actual with plan, and action on the differences” is the definition of
o: budgetary control
production budget
cash budget
zero-based budgeting
items.s: budgetary control is the setting of plans, the comparison of actual with plan, and action on the differences.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “corrective action taken on expected future results before those results occur”
o: uniform costing
feedforward control
reconciliation statement
cost ledger control account
items.s: feedforward control is corrective action taken on expected future results before those results occur.
items.t: Cost accounting systems and the cost ledger

items.q: The correct meaning of passenger journey is
o: the carrying of one traveller over the whole route once
outlay that varies with the distance covered
a schedule that gathers the fixed and variable outlay of a fleet for a period
working out the outlay of a unit of help given rather than of goods made
items.s: passenger journey: the carrying of one traveller over the whole route once. The other options describe running cost, service costing, operating cost statement.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines interlocking system?
o: two separate sets of records kept in agreement by a pair of mirror accounts
the use of common methods and terms by several firms within one industry
a single set of records that serves both the financial and the costing purposes of the firm
a working paper that spreads indirect outlay across the sections of a factory
items.s: interlocking system: two separate sets of records kept in agreement by a pair of mirror accounts. The other options describe cost apportionment sheet, integrated system, uniform costing.
items.t: Cost accounting systems and the cost ledger

items.q: In this course, reconciliation statement refers to
o: the use of common methods and terms by several firms within one industry
corrective action taken on expected future results before those results occur
a schedule that explains why two sets of records show different results for one period
a working paper that spreads indirect outlay across the sections of a factory
items.s: reconciliation statement: a schedule that explains why two sets of records show different results for one period. The other options describe feedforward control, uniform costing, cost apportionment sheet.
items.t: Cost accounting systems and the cost ledger

items.q: In this course, target costing refers to
o: the pattern in which the hours needed per item fall by a fixed proportion as output doubles
setting the allowable outlay by deducting the wanted profit from the price the market will pay
measuring one result against the best practice found elsewhere
examining what each part of an item does in order to remove needless outlay
items.s: target costing: setting the allowable outlay by deducting the wanted profit from the price the market will pay. The other options describe value analysis, benchmarking, learning curve.

items.q: The correct meaning of profit-volume ratio is
o: the amount by which actual sales exceed those needed to avoid a loss
the level of sales at which keeping going costs more than stopping
contribution expressed as a percentage of sales value
the level of activity at which neither profit nor loss arises
items.s: profit-volume ratio: contribution expressed as a percentage of sales value. The other options describe shut-down point, break-even point, margin of safety.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines standard cost?
o: a gap that increases profit compared with the plan
a gap that reduces profit compared with the plan
the planned outlay for one item, built up from technical specifications
the effect of paying above or below the planned rate for the quantities purchased
items.s: standard cost: the planned outlay for one item, built up from technical specifications. The other options describe adverse variance, material price variance, favourable variance.
